gaps.title: Documented cold-chain compliance failure, not a hypothetical risk
gaps.detail: This isn't inferred -- Maharashtra's FDA physically inspected Zepto's Dharavi warehouse and found dairy above the mandated 0-4C and frozen goods failing the -18C requirement, on top of expired stock stored alongside fresh product. The facility's license was suspended under the Food Safety and Standards Act. That's a proven gap between what's required and what was actually being monitored on the ground.
gaps.based_on: On May 31, 2025, the Maharashtra FDA inspected Zepto's Dharavi warehouse... and found... dairy products not maintained at the mandated 0-4C. Frozen items failed to meet the -18C requirement... Expired products stored alongside fresh stock... resulting in license suspension.

gaps.title: Doubling dark-store count while under heightened regulatory scrutiny
gaps.detail: Zepto plans to grow from 1,139 to roughly 3,000+ dark stores by FY30, funded by its IPO -- right as the state FDA has ordered inspections across every quick-commerce operator following Zepto's own violation. Scaling that fast without first closing the underlying monitoring gap multiplies the exposure across hundreds of new sites instead of containing it to one.
gaps.based_on: As of March 31, 2026, Zepto operated 1,139 dark stores... allocating Rs 1,629 crore to set up 1,904 new dark stores through FY30 -- nearly doubling its current footprint.

pitch.angle: This isn't a hypothetical gap -- Maharashtra's FDA already caught Zepto's Dharavi warehouse with dairy above 4C and frozen goods above -18C, on top of expired stock mixed with fresh, and suspended its license for it. The state then ordered inspections across every quick-commerce player in Maharashtra. Zepto is now trying to fund nearly 1,900 new dark stores through its IPO by FY30 -- doubling its footprint under exactly the kind of regulatory attention that makes a repeat violation a much bigger story the second time. GND's ThinxFresh gives Zepto the thing its own regulator just proved it doesn't reliably have today: instant deviation alerts and auto-generated compliance records, provable per dark store, before an inspector has to find the problem for them.
pitch.opener: After the Dharavi FDA suspension, how are you making sure the next 1,900 dark stores don't repeat the same cold-chain finding -- same manual process, or something that catches it before an inspector does?
